title: Getting started with laridae
text: triangulation described three tables every hypertidy mesher shares. square square hole, two closed rings constraint segments. vertices — x, y, attribute columns, origin vertex (input, crossing, steiner) stable id. triangles — v0, v1, v2 (1-based rows vertices table), depth depth_distinct (see ). segments — constraint edges v0, v1, input segment id came , count, number input segments covering edge.

title: Getting started with laridae
text: depth counts constraint crossings way outside convex hull. nested rings odd inside even hole, square---hole depth 1 ring depth 2 inside hole. depth_distinct count, doubled boundary — edge covered several coincident input segments — crossed instead per segment. simple ring two agree; differ boundaries duplicated (common artefact per-polygon ring data).
code: table(lari_depth(m)) #>  #> 1 2  #> 8 2

title: Getting started with laridae
text: lari_triangulate() builds, optionally refines, returns three tables one call — drop-form mirrors cdtr’s cdt_triangulate().
code: r <- lari_triangulate(x, y, s0 = 1:8, s1 = c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5),                       max_area = 0.01, min_angle = 25) plot_mesh(r, by = r$triangles$depth, main = "refined, shaded by depth")

title: Getting started with laridae
text: handle sets laridae apart: points constraints can inserted removed time, vertex ids stay stable, refinement can continue restart edit touching affected neighbourhood. Edit mesh refine — neighbourhood edit redone. advance mesher one step time last criteria.
code: m <- lari_new(x, y, s0 = 1:8, s1 = c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5)) lari_refine(m, max_area = 0.01, min_angle = 25) lari_counts(m) #> $input #> [1] 8 #>  #> $crossing #> [1] 0 #>  #> $steiner #> [1] 81 #>  #> $faces #> [1] 144 #>  #> $segments #> [1] 8 #>  #> $edges #> [1] 48 #>  #> $refined #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $mesher_alive #> [1] TRUE #>  #> $min_edge_length #> [1] 0.025 #>  #> $unrefined #>                 bad          shortEdges    sharpFixedCorner circumcenterOutside  #>                   0                   0                   0                   0  #>            inserted           budgetHit             stalled  #>                  81                   0                   0 ids <- lari_add_points(m, c(0.1, 0.15), c(0.1, 0.12)) lari_add_segments(m, ids[1], ids[2]) #> [1] 9 lari_refine(m, max_area = 0.01, min_angle = 25) lari_counts(m)$steiner #> [1] 94 lari_step(m, n = 5) #> [1] 0

what: Refinement: angle, area, and sizing fields
title: Getting started with laridae
text: Beyond global min_angle max_area, laridae takes sizing field: local maximum triangle area function position (grid). target area grows x, triangles fine left coarse right.
code: ms <- lari_new(c(0, 1, 1, 0), c(0, 0, 1, 1), 1:4, c(2, 3, 4, 1)) lari_refine(ms, size = function(x, y) 0.0005 + 0.01 * x) plot_mesh(lari_tables(ms), main = "sizing field: fine on the left")

title: Getting started with laridae
text: Per-vertex attributes passed PA carried onto crossings Steiner points linear interpolation, field defined inputs stays consistent refinement.
code: z <- 2 * x + 3 * y + 1   # a linear field on the inputs ra <- lari_triangulate(x, y, 1:8, c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5),                        PA = cbind(z = z), max_area = 0.01) ## a linear field is reproduced exactly at every vertex max(abs(ra$vertices$z - (2 * ra$vertices$x + 3 * ra$vertices$y + 1))) #> [1] 8.881784e-16

title: Constrained Triangulation and Meshing with CGAL
text: lari_triangulate() one-shot form, returning three tables like cdtr’s cdt_triangulate(). Per-vertex attributes (PA = cbind(z_ = z)) ride along: crossings Steiner points get linearly interpolated values.
code: library(laridae) ## a square with a square hole: two closed rings of segments x <- c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75, 0.25) y <- c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0.25, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75) m <- lari_new(x, y, s0 = 1:8, s1 = c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5)) table(lari_depth(m))        # 1 = in the outer ring, 2 = in the hole  lari_refine(m, max_area = 0.01, min_angle = 25) lari_counts(m)  ## edit and re-refine: only the neighbourhood of the edit is touched ids <- lari_add_points(m, c(0.1, 0.15), c(0.1, 0.12)) lari_add_segments(m, ids[1], ids[2]) lari_refine(m, max_area = 0.01, min_angle = 25)  ## or one point at a time lari_step(m, n = 10)  ## a sizing field: local maximum area as a function of position m2 <- lari_new(c(0, 1, 1, 0), c(0, 0, 1, 1), 1:4, c(2, 3, 4, 1)) lari_refine(m2, size = function(x, y) 0.0005 + 0.01 * x)  ## the contract tables lari_vertices(m)    # x, y, attributes, origin (input/crossing/steiner), id lari_triangles(m)   # v0, v1, v2 (rows of the vertices table), depth lari_segments(m)    # v0, v1, input segment id, count of covering segments

title: Refine a mesh — lari_refine
text: Ruppert-style Delaunay refinement CGAL's Delaunay_mesher_2, minimum angle, maximum area, sizing field. mesher kept handle lari_step() can continue one point time; edit mesh discards .

title: Refine a mesh — lari_refine
code: lari_refine(   m,   min_angle = NULL,   max_area = NULL,   size = NULL,   max_steiner = Inf,   min_edge_length = NULL,   seeds = NULL,   erase = c("outer", "holes", "hull") )

title: Refine a mesh — lari_refine
text: m mesh lari_new() min_angle minimum triangle angle degrees, NULL none. 20.7 degrees termination guaranteed theory; floor keeps finite. max_area maximum triangle area, NULL none size sizing field giving local maximum triangle area: function(x, y) (called scalars triangle centroid), grid list(x, y, z) graphics::image() convention (x y cell centres, z length(x) length(y); nearest cell, NA unbounded). Combined max_area taking smaller bound. max_steiner budget new vertices call (Inf none) min_edge_length edge-length floor; NULL chooses default_min_edge_length() current segments area bound, taking smaller max_area finest area sizing field asks sizing field honoured rather capped; 0 never gives seeds optional points (two-column matrix list x, y) marking regions mesh, CGAL style; given replace erase erase region meshed: "outer" (everything inside outermost constraints, depth > 0), "holes" (odd depth ), "hull"

title: laridae 0.1.0
text: Rebuilt scratch CGAL 6 (Constrained_triangulation_plus_2 exact predicates Delaunay_mesher_2) behind persistent cpp11 handle: lari_new(), lari_add_points(), lari_add_segments(), lari_remove_points(), lari_remove_segments(), lari_refine(), lari_step(), contract tables lari_vertices(), lari_triangles(), lari_segments(), lari_depth(), lari_counts(). Sizing fields: lari_refine(size = ) takes function position grid giving local maximum triangle area. default edge-length floor now accounts sizing field, size argument honoured instead capped coarse input-edge scale min_edge_length left default. Hull-edge Steiner points created refinement now get attributes interpolated along nearest hull edge, rather copied single nearest vertex (fixes attribute error map scale). lari_triangles() (lari_tables()) gain depth_distinct column: constraint depth doubled boundary counted , matching cdtr’s depth_distinct. lari_tables() lari_triangulate() now return one-row report backend, laridae CGAL versions, erase region, edge floor, last refinement’s unrefined counts. Licence now GPL (>= 3), required CGAL’s Mesh_2. CGAL (>= 6.0) Boost headers supplied CRAN packages RcppCGAL BH via LinkingTo, system CGAL required compiled code passes R CMD check ---cran. development, set CGAL_INCLUDE_DIR build stock CGAL headers instead (see README; route CRAN-clean). Builds macOS Windows: CGAL 6’s Constrained_triangulation_plus_2 includes boost/stl_interfaces/iterator_interface.hpp, BH ship, three Boost.STLInterfaces headers needs vendored src/boost-extra (Boost Software License). Linux built system Boost filled gap. Windows also gets src/Makevars.win. previous Rcpp/cgalh code preserved legacy-rcpp branch.
